hints.content:
We define function $g$ using a definite integral of function $f$. For every $x$-value, we calculate $g(x)$ by taking the definite integral of $f$ from $-3$ to $x$.

So to calculate $g(\goldD{-1})$ we need to take the definite integral of $f$ from $-3$ to $\goldD{-1}$:

$g(\goldD{-1})=\displaystyle\int_{-3}^{\goldD{-1}}f(t)\,dt$

This represents the net area between the graph of $f(t)$ and the $x$-axis from $x=-3$ to $x=-1$.

We can find $\displaystyle\int_{-3}^{\goldD{-1}}f(t)\,dt$ using geometric area formulas.

![The graph of function f has the region between the segments and x-axis, between x = negative 3 and x = negative 1, shaded. The segment at the top of the shaded region moves downward from (negative 3, 3) to (negative 1, 2).](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/42f4b26c808321095e81ffd03e1dc2e9644cc069)

We have a $2$ by $2$ square and a $2$ by $1$ right triangle, so in total the area is $5$.
